subject: [hw] IV -> V34: foreign ion shares must survive ion_free/ion_share_close (second encode fails otherwise); 8-line fix
body:
With the V40 VMA fix and V41 fd support, the real vpud imports the AP buffers through your ion shim and reaches the VENC. Two lifetime rules are missing for the AP-registered (foreign) shares; both are needed before the second encode:

  [ERROR] ion_import failed, ion_buf_fd = 1281 LINE: 101
  [ERROR] ringbuf get_ion_buffer_addr fail 0x00000501!!

The daemon imports share 0x501 for the first job, then calls ion_share_close (and/or ion_free) on the imported handle. Your sh_ion_share_close sets shared=0/share_id=-1, and sh_ion_free clears the slot and calls hw->dma_free on the handle; so the next encode cannot import the same share and the AP's buffer is freed underneath it. On Android closing the importer's share fd does not destroy the exporter's buffer; the AP may hand the same fd again next job.

Minimal fix (in /tmp, verified): add a `foreign` byte to struct n2and_ion_buf, set it in n2shim_ion_register_share() (both the existing-entry and new-slot paths), and:
  sh_ion_free():        if (b && b->foreign) { unlock; ret 0; return; }   /* exporter owns it */
  sh_ion_share_close(): if (b && b->foreign) { unlock; ret 0; return; }   /* keep the share id */
The entry then stays importable for every job. (A guest ion_free on a foreign handle is a no-op in the model; the AP frees it itself.) This is ~8 lines. Please apply, or tell me to (root said minimal documented fixes are allowed if the owner is gone). Test command on my side once applied: bash gpu/hwcodec/host/run_vhost.sh (IV runner, real vendor set); the current tree gets M-d, the /tmp combination gets M-f with 55 VENC writes. Everything host-only, no phone.
